contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_program (D3D8/D3D9 vertex shaders 1.1-2.0 through Wine's ARB backend)
contracts.operation: VERTEX_PROGRAM_ARB objects in the shared program namespace, ProgramString with error position/string, env/local parameters, VERTEX_PROGRAM_ARB/POINT_SIZE/TWO_SIDE enables, generic attributes (VertexAttrib*ARB outside and inside Begin/End and in display lists, client arrays through the attribute draw), attribute 0 aliasing the position, program/attribute/limit queries, ENABLE_BIT/CURRENT_BIT/CLIENT_VERTEX_ARRAY_BIT
contracts.format: ARBvp1.0 ASCII program strings up to DG_GL_MAX_PROGRAM_BYTES; 16 generic attributes of every GL 1.1 component type, sizes 1-4, normalized or not
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_PROGRAM; without it the extension and entry points are hidden and vertex program modes stay GL_INVALID_ENUM. Generic client arrays travel in their own DATA record (the VertexAttribPointerARB function number, 16 conventional and 16 generic descriptors), so older kernels keep their DrawArrays/DrawArraysEXT admission. Attribute 0 is the position (the non-aliasing GL 2.0 model Mesa implements): its array supersedes the vertex array and generic attributes 1-15 never alias conventional ones. Host checks reject non-ASCII bytes and vertex.attrib[n] at or beyond MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS_ARB (16); other semantic limits are native. Every vertex load goes into a fresh native object that replaces the program's on success (Mesa 26.1 frees a serialized program twice when one vertex object is translated three times). Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa on Radeon) cover env-parameter transforms, every generic array type and size, current values inside and outside Begin/End, position aliasing, program matrices and state.matrix.mvp, per-vertex point size, two-sided colours, relative addressing, parse and host-detected failures, invalid-program draws, display lists, ENABLE_BIT/CURRENT_BIT, combined vertex and fragment programs, sharing/isolation, and the vs_1_1/vs_2_0 programs WineD3D generates for the installed probe. Wine patch 0033 maps glVertexAttrib2svARB, clamps VS 2.0 NumTemps, sets VERTEX_PROGRAM_POINT_SIZE only for oPts writers, disables vertex programs for CPU depth uploads and binds the zero attribute as a client array without ARB_vertex_buffer_object. Expected caps: D3D9 VertexShaderVersion 2.0 with 256 constants, D3D8 1.1. VS 2.0 makes Wine report its NVIDIA fallback for that level, a GeForce FX 5800 (10de:0302, previously a GeForce 256), whose quirk enabled the rectangle textures DreamGPU lacks and blacked out DirectDraw/D3D6/D3D7 presentation until patch 0034. The installed D3D8/9 vertex shader probe (vs_1_1 for two constant sets, vs_2_0 on D3D9, vs_1_1 into ps_1_1) passes on Win2000, XP and Win98 SE (Linux host). Signed normalized generic arrays convert natively (c/32767) while immediate and ArrayElement 4N values follow GL 1.x; D3D point size limits, ARB_vertex_buffer_object, macOS CGL and games using vertex shaders remain unverified.

contracts.format: uncompressed internal formats; every 2D wire format and GL 1.2 packed type
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_TEXTURE_3D; without it the extension, entry points, enums and image pixel storage stay hidden. TexImage3D/TexSubImage3D are nine- and ten-word DATA records with tight payloads (the frontend resolves every unpack value and splits into bounded slabs of whole images or 2D tiles); CopyTexSubImage3D is a nine-word CALL. MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE is 256; images are borderless (a border is GL_INVALID_OPERATION, its proxy rejected) and compressed 3D formats are not accepted. Native pixel tests (Linux, private Mesa on Radeon) sample slices at explicit R with NEAREST and LINEAR filtering, mip levels, WRAP_R, subimages, copies, readback through every image, zero definitions, tight RGB and packed payloads, proxies, display lists, per-unit bindings and TEXTURE_BIT, 3D over 2D precedence and the incomplete fallback. Wine claims VOLUMEMAP, MIPVOLUMEMAP and VOLUMEMAP_POW2; patch 0035 states the unpack alignment of volume uploads. The installed D3D8/9 volume probe (four LockBox slices of a MANAGED A8R8G8B8 4x4x4 texture) is untested on guests; DEFAULT-pool LockBox, volume mip chains through D3D, converted formats, shaders sampling volumes, macOS CGL and games remain unverified.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_buffer_object (D3D8/D3D9 vertex and index buffers through Wine)
contracts.operation: ARRAY_BUFFER/ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER objects in the shared namespace: Gen/Delete/Is/Bind, BufferData (all usage hints), BufferSubData, GetBufferSubData, Map/Unmap, GetBufferParameteriv/Pointerv; array pointers latching buffer offsets (conventional, units 1-7, fog, generic attributes, InterleavedArrays), *_ARRAY_BUFFER_BINDING queries, DrawArrays/DrawElements from buffers, ArrayElement, display list dereference
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_BUFFER_OBJECT; without it the extension and entry points are hidden and every draw is unchanged. BufferData/BufferSubData/DeleteBuffers name their buffer and execute immediately (never compiled); contents up to DG_GL_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES travel in bounded BufferSubData slabs and are charged against the resource budget. Bindings, array latches and mappings are frontend client state; the frontend keeps a copy of every buffer, so maps return it (16-byte aligned), Unmap re-sends it unless READ_ONLY, and reads never wait for the host. Draws reading buffers use the buffer draw (DATA function DrawRangeElements: references per slot, client sections of the indexed vertex range, inline or element-buffer indices), so older kernels keep every existing admission; the host bounds every read against current sizes, scanning element-buffer indices in its own copy, and state-dependent failures are GL errors. Display list compilation and anything the record cannot express (unaligned offsets, strides beyond 2048, oversized client sections) dereference the buffers into client draws. BufferData on a mapped buffer unmaps it, as in Mesa; buffers deleted in another context end its draws with GL_INVALID_OPERATION. Wine patches 0037-0040 double-buffer buffer objects with dirty-range BufferSubData uploads, repair this tree's fixed-function D3DCOLOR/XYZRHW conversion, keep immediate mode on memory and size/delete the zero attribute buffer; dynamic buffers stay in system memory without ARB_map_buffer_range. Native pixel tests, the installed D3D8/9 vertex buffer probe, macOS CGL and games remain to be run on guests.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + EXT_framebuffer_object, EXT_framebuffer_blit, EXT_packed_depth_stencil (D3D8/D3D9 render targets through Wine ORM_FBO)
contracts.operation: framebuffer objects per context and renderbuffers in the shared namespace: Gen/Delete/Is/Bind (FRAMEBUFFER, DRAW/READ_FRAMEBUFFER), RenderbufferStorage, FramebufferTexture1D/2D/3D (cube faces, 3D slices), FramebufferRenderbuffer, CheckFramebufferStatus, GetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv, GetRenderbufferParameteriv, GenerateMipmap, BlitFramebuffer, per-framebuffer draw/read buffers, binding queries, ReadPixels/CopyTex*/CopyPixels from objects, 2D depth and packed depth/stencil textures
contracts.format: RGB/RGBA sized colour, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24/32, STENCIL_INDEX1-16, DEPTH24_STENCIL8
contracts.usage: render target, depth-stencil and blit source/destination
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_FRAMEBUFFER_OBJECT; without it the extensions, entry points and enums stay hidden. Framebuffer names are virtual and per context; zero stays the host's drawable framebuffer, rebound by the host under the guest's objects on every make-current, exchange and export, so presentation and window readback are unchanged with an object bound. Every command but BlitFramebuffer executes immediately; state-dependent failures are GL errors and completeness is the native GL 3 rules (no INCOMPLETE_DIMENSIONS/FORMATS). Attachments keep deleted images alive until detached; rendering into them is fenced for other contexts and versioned for the texture read cache. Renderbuffers are zero-initialized and charged against the resource budget; reads of uninitialized images are INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION; ReadPixels from an object is clipped by the host to its attachments. 2D textures take depth and packed depth/stencil formats for depth attachments; ARB_depth_texture and depth GetTexImage are not claimed. Wine selects ORM_FBO, and with this tree's always_offscreen every D3D8/9 swapchain renders into an FBO and presents with glBlitFramebuffer; patches 0042-0046 keep NPOT resources in padded 2D textures, give CPU depth transfers an FBO mode, attach larger depth buffers directly, send overlapping self-blits to the CPU blitter and keep point sprites upright through POINT_SPRITE_COORD_ORIGIN below GL 2.0. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D8/9 render-target probe, the existing probes under ORM_FBO, adapter-start format checks (R5G6B5 targets, blending), macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_vertex_array_bgra (D3DCOLOR vertex streams through Wine)
contracts.operation: size BGRA for ColorPointer, SecondaryColorPointerEXT and VertexAttribPointerARB (normalized); its errors; BGRA size queries and CLIENT_VERTEX_ARRAY_BIT; client-memory, buffer-object, display list and ArrayElement draws
contracts.usage: diffuse, specular and generic vertex attributes
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BGRA; without it BGRA stays an invalid size and every draw is unchanged. The frontend reorders client memory into the RGBA sections of the existing array records (a secondary colour as RGB), so older records, kernels and hosts keep their admission; a draw with a BGRA buffer slot uses the BGRA buffer draw (DATA function DrawRangeElementsEXT: the buffer draw plus DG_GL_ARRAY_BGRA on colour, secondary colour and generic buffer slots), which the NT/Win9x kernels and the host check like the buffer draw and which native GL reads with size BGRA. Lists and the record's fallbacks dereference buffers into reordered client draws. Wine then draws fixed-function D3DCOLOR diffuse/specular streams outside buffer objects (D3D8/9 UP, dynamic and SYSTEMMEM buffers, D3D5-7 user memory and system-memory vertex buffers) from arrays instead of immediate mode, stops converting D3DCOLOR in buffer objects, and feeds vertex shaders GL_BGRA generic arrays; Wine 0048 draws XYZRHW streams outside buffer objects from arrays too (positions converted as immediate mode converted them, colours in place as GL_BGRA). Wine 0047 fixes the stride-zero D3DCOLOR zero attribute. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D7 and D3D8/9 colour-array and XYZRHW probes, macOS CGL (EXT_vertex_array_bgra), Win98/XP guests and game performance remain to be run.

contracts.api: OpenGL 1.1 + ARB_occlusion_query and NV_fence (D3D9 occlusion and event queries through Wine)
contracts.operation: Gen/Delete/Is/Begin/EndQuery, GetQueryiv (CURRENT_QUERY, QUERY_COUNTER_BITS), GetQueryObject(u)iv (RESULT, RESULT_AVAILABLE) and their errors; Gen/Delete/Set/Test/Finish/IsFenceNV and GetFenceivNV; display lists
contracts.remaining: Negotiated by DG_CAP_GL_OCCLUSION_QUERY; without it the extensions and entry points stay hidden and every entry point fails locally. Query and fence objects belong to one context and the host owns names, objects and the active query; BeginQuery, EndQuery and SetFenceNV compile into display lists, deletion executes immediately, and every state-dependent failure (nesting, Gen/Delete while active, results of non-objects or the active query) is a GL error. Results stay asynchronous on the host: a pending availability or fence status flushes native GL, QUERY_RESULT and FinishFenceNV wait, and one GetQueryObject round trip carries the result and the results of earlier ended queries, which the frontend keeps with signalled fences until the name is begun, set or deleted or a list executes. Objects are charged against the resource budget, at most 4096 names per kind and context. Wine then creates D3DQUERYTYPE_OCCLUSION queries (D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE before) and backs D3DQUERYTYPE_EVENT with NV fences (an issued event's GetData failed with D3DERR_INVALIDCALL before); this Wine still answers a pending event S_OK with FALSE. Native pixel tests pass on Linux; the installed D3D9 query probe, macOS CGL, Win98/XP guests and games remain to be run.
